title: Chapter 105: Second Haunted House Worker!
html:
As Wang Xin read the words, emotion overwhelmed her. She slowly leaned forward and reached for the pen in Chen Ge’s hand.

Her cold fingers slipped between his palm and the pen, her arm trembling as if she had not felt another person’s warmth in years. She tried to speak, but no voice came. As the three minutes ended, the pen moved between their hands and wrote only two words: “Good night.”

The pen fell still. Chen Ge recited the farewell incantation, and Wang Xin involuntarily followed. “Pen Spirit, Pen Spirit, you are my spirit from my previous life, and I am your spirit in this life. If you wish to go, then please go ahead.”

As they spoke the final word, the dam inside Wang Xin broke. The needle buried in her heart for years finally came free. She clutched Chen Ge’s hands and turned her face away, unwilling to let anyone witness her pain.

“All the lights in the world went out, and everyone fell silent. What was I supposed to do alone? Every feeling was wrong, and every path ended in a dead end. I didn’t understand what I had done, but somehow I became a monster.” At last, Wang Xin released the words trapped inside her. She stared at the message on the paper, then bent forward as her voice faded. “Help me. Pull me out of this world. I want to be free of this pain. Please…”

Her forehead rested against the back of Chen Ge’s hands as she sank onto the mattress. Her breathing steadied. For the first time in what must have been years, Wang Xin fell asleep.

“Good night.”

Chen Ge gently withdrew his hand, covered Wang Xin with a quilt, and left the room. Doctor Gao and her adoptive mother waited outside. Eager to know what had happened but afraid to wake her, they whispered their questions.

“How is Wang Xin?”

Chen Ge pointed into the bedroom. “She’s asleep.”

“She’s really sleeping?” Doctor Gao breathed. He knew how difficult sleep was for severely traumatized patients without medication. “How did you do it?”

“It’s a long story.” Chen Ge offered a partial truth. “While researching Mu Yang High School for my Haunted House, I found information about Wang Xin’s past and learned what caused her condition. Watching her friend die during a Pen Spirit game left a wound she could never process. I recreated the game she once played with her roommates and used it to show her that the death was an accident, not her fault.”

“And it worked?” Doctor Gao was impressed.

The woman behind him had tears in her eyes. “Thank you. I’m sorry I doubted you.”

“There’s no need to apologize. You and Doctor Gao have done far more than I did. Neither of you abandoned Wang Xin when she needed help most. That is what mattered.” His generous praise improved their opinion of him. Wang Xin’s adoptive mother invited them to stay for a meal, but Chen Ge declined. The black phone had vibrated twice when Wang Xin fell asleep, and he was anxious to read its messages.

Outside Fang Hwa, Chen Ge said goodbye to Doctor Gao and boarded a bus to New Century Park. He took a seat in the back row and, once sure no one was watching, drew out the black phone.

“Congratulations on completing the Two-Star Scenario Mu Yang High School’s Hidden Mission: The Pen Spirit’s Wish! The next stage has been activated. Create mannequins for the twenty-four spirits to possess!

“The Pen Spirit’s Wish has been completed. Although she still cannot see you, she is grateful for your help. Would you like to recruit the Pen Spirit as an employee of the Haunted House?”

Chen Ge selected “Yes” without hesitation. He had waited far too long for this opportunity.

“Specters’ Favored, congratulations on recruiting a Special-Type Baleful Specter: the Pen Spirit!

“Chen Yalin (Pen Spirit): One fortune-telling opportunity per day. All questions must fall within the Pen Spirit’s power. The chance of a successful reading is fifty percent.

“Note: The Pen Spirit feeds on visitors’ frightened screams. Their fear will strengthen her, but if she remains isolated and unhappy, she may decide to leave.”

Chen Ge reread the information, barely containing his excitement. At last, he had recruited his first supernatural employee. His old dream was becoming possible: a theme park he could operate entirely on his own.

A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step. I’m sure more ghosts will join my team in the future.Chen Ge was very satisfied with the Pen Spirit. She could handle a small scenario all on her own, and her special talent could be incredibly useful.

The next stage of Mu Yang High School’s Hidden Mission required mannequins for the sealed classroom’s lingering spirits to possess. Even without the black phone’s instructions, Chen Ge would eventually have done the same.

His conversation with Inspector Lee had explained why the twenty-four students returned to their classroom. They were orphans, and Mu Yang High School had been their home. When the scenario unlocked, they effectively moved into Chen Ge’s Haunted House, much like Xiaoxiao’s family.

As I complete more Trial Missions, the underground scenario will only get bigger; I will need the help of these twenty-four lingering spirits to manage the sets. We both need the other.Chen Ge’s plan was nice, but he needed to get the goodwill of the twenty-four spirits first.

The moment he returned to the Haunted House, Chen Ge went to sleep, exhausted by the day’s events. Some time later, something crawled across his chest like a kitten demanding attention. He opened his eyes and found himself hugging a small doll.

“Xiaoxiao?” He rubbed his eyes and set her beside him. “What are you doing? I’m a grown man. Imagine what my future wife will think if she catches me sleeping with a doll.”

He stretched and checked the time: 11:59 p.m. Pulling on his shoes, he left the staff break room for the first-floor bathroom.

He only needed to relieve himself, but the moment he entered, he sensed something wrong. The cubicle door swayed gently, and a red glow seeped from beneath the black cloth covering the mirror.

Has the door in the mirror returned?

He approached the mirror and lifted one corner of the cloth.

Within the cracked glass, the red door stood half-open.
